title: A reviewer's verdict on one pull request (agents/reviewer.md)

commit.description: The pull request's head commit on GitHub, which the review read; never the local merge with main.

round.description: Counted since the issue last left Escalated (agents/README.md). Round 2 checks round 1's blocking and fix_now findings and the lines changed since; round 3 checks only the blocking findings that round 2 left open and the lines changed since round 2.

summary.description: Two or three sentences: what the pull request does and why the verdict is what it is.

decision.description: With needs-decision: the question for the owner, with the options, or the gate the reviewer could not run and why, when nothing else blocks. In round 1 or 2 with a blocking finding open, the verdict is request-changes, and summary names the gate that did not run and why.

issue.description: With approve: the follow-up issue that took the lines (its identifier, as `linear.py follow-up` prints it), when at least one finding has follow_up true or a fix_now finding of round 1 is still open (agents/README.md 'Follow-ups'). When every such finding needs the owner's choice, each got its own issue with a Question: blocker: then the key of one of those issues.

previous.description: Rounds 2 and 3: each finding that the round before left open (round 2: each blocking and each fix_now finding of round 1; round 3: each blocking finding that round 2 left open), and whether it is fixed.

fix_now.description: True for a fix_now finding of round 1: still open, it does not stop an approve and becomes a line of the follow-up issue.

gates.description: The gates the reviewer ran on the branch merged with main (agents/reviewer.md 'The gates'). Required when the pull request has no required checks (the `gates` workflow is disabled, or its `python` and `web` checks never ran on the head commit: agents/README.md 'Green'); left out when those checks ran. Empty only when .github/code-changed.sh prints false for the file names of the diff against main. When it prints true: the gate that the product's AGENTS.md names for each kind of file of the diff.

command.description: The command as run, for example `mise run gates`.

exit_code.description: The command's exit code: 0 passes, anything else fails.

id.description: Stable across rounds: R1-1, R1-2, ... R2-1.

blocking.description: True only when the finding meets the merge bar (AGENTS.md 'Autonomous runs').

bar.description: With blocking: which part of the merge bar it meets.

failure.description: The concrete inputs or state, and the wrong result.

fix.description: What a correct fix must do.

confirmed.description: False when the reviewer could not confirm the finding in the code or by a run: such a finding is never blocking.

follow_up.description: Non-blocking only: true when the finding passes the floor (a person would schedule it; a finding about a property of the merge bar always does, confirmed or not) and becomes a line of the follow-up issue, or its own issue with a Question: blocker when its fix needs the owner's choice; a non-blocking finding is either this or fix_now: a finding nobody acts on (a preference) is not written. At most five true per verdict.

fix_now.description: Round 1 only, non-blocking and confirmed: the fix is XS (any size on a docs-only pull request), stays in files the pull request already changes, and needs no choice the issue did not make. It makes the verdict request-changes, and the implementer fixes it in the fix round (agents/README.md 'Follow-ups').

allOf.$comment: a blocking finding is not a follow-up
every finding is acted on: a non-blocking one is fix_now or a follow-up line
a fix_now finding is confirmed, not blocking, and not a follow-up line
rounds 2 and 3 mark no finding fix_now
approve: no blocking or fix_now finding open, every blocking finding of round 1 fixed (a fix_now one may stay open), and every gate run passed
request-changes: round 1 or round 2; round 3 with a blocking finding open is needs-decision
round 1 asks for changes for a blocking or a fix_now finding
round 2 asks for changes only for a blocking finding: a new one, or one of round 1 still open (not fix_now)
